_doc: Nepal, written by hand for the recommended trips (Manu, 2026-11-16): the Kathmandu valley, Pokhara, Chitwan, Lumbini, a night in each village of the Everest, Poon Hill and Annapurna Sanctuary treks, and Mustang for the monsoon. Nepal has required a licensed guide on most trekking routes since 2023. Sources per area; scores on docs/RANKING.md.

areas.season: At 1,300 m: warm and dusty October to May, monsoon rain June to September, cold mornings December to February.
areas.sleep: Thamel for trekkers, or the quieter lanes around Patan's Durbar Square or Boudha.

items.name: Kathmandu Durbar Square and the old bazaars
items.why: The old royal square of temples and palaces, part of UNESCO's Kathmandu Valley site, the house of the living goddess Kumari, and the bazaar of Asan.

items.name: Pashupatinath and Boudhanath
items.why: Open-air cremations on the Bagmati at Nepal's holiest Hindu temple, then the kora at dusk around Boudhanath, one of the largest stupas in the world.

items.name: Swayambhunath, the monkey temple
items.why: 365 steps up a hill to a white stupa with the Buddha's eyes, prayer wheels, monkeys and the whole valley below.

items.name: Patan Durbar Square and museum
items.why: The finest of the valley's royal squares, with Newar temples of brick and carved wood and one of Asia's best small museums in the palace.

items.name: Mountain flight to Everest
items.why: An hour along the Himalaya at dawn, with Everest from the cockpit, for those not trekking to it.

areas.season: As Kathmandu: warm October to May, monsoon June to September.
areas.sleep: Guesthouses on the squares of the old town.

items.name: Bhaktapur's squares and the potters
items.why: A car-free Newar town of temples: the five-storey Nyatapola, the 55-window palace, potters' square and the king curd, juju dhau.

items.name: Changu Narayan temple
items.why: The oldest temple of the valley, from the 4th century, on a ridge 6 km north of Bhaktapur.

areas.season: At 2,100 m: the clearest views October to February; cold nights in winter, cloud in the monsoon.
areas.sleep: Hotels along the ridge, facing north.

items.name: Himalaya sunrise
items.why: From the ridge the Himalaya from Annapurna to Everest, 200 km of snow peaks turning pink at dawn.

items.name: Walk down to Changu Narayan
items.why: Along the ridge through pine forest and villages to the valley's oldest temple, then a bus to Bhaktapur.

areas.season: At 1,550 m: as Nagarkot, the Himalaya clearest October to February.
areas.sleep: Lodges on the ridge above the old town.

items.name: Walk to Namobuddha monastery
items.why: Through terraced villages to the hilltop monastery where the young Buddha gave himself to a starving tigress.

items.name: Panauti old town
items.why: A Newar town at the meeting of two rivers, its temples untouched by the tourists of the valley.

areas.season: At 1,000 m: warm, with Himalaya views October to February.
areas.sleep: Guesthouses in the old Newar houses of the bazaar.

items.name: Bandipur bazaar and Tundikhel
items.why: A car-free hill town of 18th-century Newar trading houses, and the meadow of Tundikhel with the Annapurnas and Manaslu at dawn.

items.name: Siddha Cave
items.why: A steep path down to one of Nepal's biggest caves, lit by your guide's lamp.

areas.season: At 800 m under the Annapurnas: warm. October to April for the mountain views; June to September is the wettest place in Nepal.

items.name: Sunrise at Sarangkot
items.why: Up before dawn to the ridge at 1,600 m: Dhaulagiri, the Annapurnas and the fishtail of Machapuchare over the lake.

items.name: Boat on Phewa lake and the Peace Pagoda
items.why: Row to the island temple of Tal Barahi, cross the lake and climb through forest to the white World Peace Pagoda.

items.name: Paragliding from Sarangkot
items.why: One of the world's great tandem flights: 30 minutes over the lake facing the Annapurnas.

items.name: International Mountain Museum
items.why: The story of the Himalaya, its peoples and the first ascents of the 8,000 m peaks.

areas.season: Hot lowlands at 200 m: the best months are October to March (foggy mornings in December and January); April to June is very hot; in the monsoon many jungle activities stop.
areas.sleep: Lodges in Sauraha by the Rapti river.

items.name: Jeep safari in Chitwan
items.hours: Half a day to a day
items.why: Grassland and sal forest of the one-horned rhino, about 700 of them; also sloth bears, gharials and, with luck, a Bengal tiger.

items.name: Dugout canoe and a jungle walk
items.why: Down the Rapti in a dugout past mugger crocodiles and kingfishers, then on foot with two naturalists.

items.name: Tharu village and dance
items.why: The people of the Terai's forests: mud-walled houses by day, stick dances in the evening.

areas.season: Hot plains: October to March; April to June reaches 40 °C.
areas.sleep: Hotels near the sacred garden, or a monastery guesthouse.

items.name: Maya Devi temple and the monasteries
items.why: The birthplace of the Buddha, on UNESCO's list, with Ashoka's pillar of 249 BC, and temples built by Buddhist countries from Japan to Germany along a canal.

areas.season: October and November are clear and dry; March to May bring rhododendrons and haze. December to February are cold but clear; June to September is the monsoon: cloud, rain and leeches below 3,000 m.

items.name: From Nayapul up the stone steps to Ulleri
items.why: From Pokhara by road to Nayapul, along the river past Birethanti, then about 3,300 stone steps up to the Magar village of Ulleri at 2,000 m.

areas.season: October and November are clear and dry; March to May bring rhododendrons and haze. December to February are cold but clear; June to September is the monsoon: cloud, rain and leeches below 3,000 m.

items.name: Through the rhododendron forest to Ghorepani
items.why: Up through forests of rhododendron, red in March and April, to the pass village under Poon Hill.

items.name: Poon Hill at sunrise
items.why: An hour up by headlamp to 3,210 m for the sun rising over Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South and Machapuchare: the classic Himalaya view.

areas.season: October and November are clear and dry; March to May bring rhododendrons and haze. December to February are cold but clear; June to September is the monsoon: cloud, rain and leeches below 3,000 m.

items.name: Over the ridge to Tadapani
items.why: From Poon Hill along the forest ridge of Deurali at 3,100 m and down to Tadapani, face to face with Machapuchare.

areas.season: October and November are clear and dry; March to May bring rhododendrons and haze. December to February are cold but clear; June to September is the monsoon: cloud, rain and leeches below 3,000 m.

items.name: Down to Ghandruk, the Gurung village
items.why: A big Gurung village of slate roofs on terraces, home of many Gurkha soldiers, with a small museum of their life.

areas.season: October and November are clear and dry; March to May bring rhododendrons and haze. December to February are cold but clear; June to September is the monsoon: cloud, rain and leeches below 3,000 m.

items.name: Across the valley to Chhomrong
items.why: The last Gurung village before the Annapurna Sanctuary, on a spur under Annapurna South and Hiunchuli.

areas.season: October and November are clear and dry; March to May bring rhododendrons and haze. December to February are cold but clear; June to September is the monsoon: cloud, rain and leeches below 3,000 m.

items.name: Down Chhomrong's steps and into the gorge to Bamboo
items.why: Down some 2,500 stone steps, across the river, up to Sinuwa and into the bamboo forest of the Modi Khola gorge.

areas.season: October and November are clear and dry; March to May bring rhododendrons and haze. December to February are cold but clear; June to September is the monsoon: cloud, rain and leeches below 3,000 m.

items.name: Up the gorge to Deurali
items.why: Out of the forest into the narrow gorge under the walls of Hiunchuli; in winter and spring watch for avalanche warnings here.

areas.season: October and November are clear and dry; March to May bring rhododendrons and haze. December to February are cold but clear; June to September is the monsoon: cloud, rain and leeches below 3,000 m.
areas.sleep: Teahouses at Annapurna Base Camp, 4,130 m.

items.name: Into the Annapurna Sanctuary
items.why: Past Machapuchare Base Camp into a ring of peaks over 6,000 m, Annapurna I (8,091 m) at its head; sunrise at base camp is the reward.

areas.season: October and November are clear and dry; March to May bring rhododendrons and haze. December to February are cold but clear; June to September is the monsoon: cloud, rain and leeches below 3,000 m.

items.name: Down to the Jhinu hot springs
items.why: The long way down from the sanctuary ends in hot pools by the Modi Khola, ten minutes below the village.

areas.season: October and November are clear and dry; March to May bring rhododendrons and haze. December to February are cold but clear; June to September is the monsoon: cloud, rain and leeches below 3,000 m.

items.name: Fly to Lukla, walk down to Phakding
items.why: A dawn flight onto Lukla's short sloping runway (from Ramechhap in the busy months), then down the Dudh Kosi past prayer walls to Phakding.

areas.season: October and November are clear and dry; March to May bring rhododendrons and haze. December to February are cold but clear; June to September is the monsoon: cloud, rain and leeches below 3,000 m.

items.name: Up to Namche Bazaar
items.why: Over high suspension bridges and up the long Namche hill, with the first glimpse of Everest, to the Sherpa capital.

items.name: Everest View Hotel and Khumjung
items.why: The day to adapt to the height: up to 3,880 m for Everest, Lhotse and Ama Dablam, then the Sherpa village of Khumjung and down.

items.name: Sherpa museum and Namche's market
items.why: Sherpa life and the history of Everest climbs, and on Saturdays the market where traders come over from Tibet's side.

areas.season: October and November are clear and dry; March to May bring rhododendrons and haze. December to February are cold but clear; June to September is the monsoon: cloud, rain and leeches below 3,000 m.

items.name: Tengboche monastery and on to Pangboche
items.why: Up through forest to Tengboche, the great monastery of the Khumbu with Everest behind it, then Pangboche under Ama Dablam.

areas.season: October and November are clear and dry; March to May bring rhododendrons and haze. December to February are cold but clear; June to September is the monsoon: cloud, rain and leeches below 3,000 m.

items.name: Into the Imja valley to Dingboche
items.why: Above the trees, among stone-walled potato fields, to the village under Island Peak and Lhotse's south face.

items.name: Nangkartshang for the height
items.why: The rest day: climb high and sleep low, up to about 5,000 m with Makalu, the world's fifth peak, in view.

areas.season: October and November are clear and dry; March to May bring rhododendrons and haze. December to February are cold but clear; June to September is the monsoon: cloud, rain and leeches below 3,000 m.
areas.sleep: Teahouses in Lobuche at 4,940 m: cold nights.

items.name: Up the moraine to Lobuche
items.why: Up the Khumbu glacier's moraine past the memorial cairns of Thukla pass, to Lobuche at about 4,940 m.

areas.season: October and November are clear and dry; March to May bring rhododendrons and haze. December to February are cold but clear; June to September is the monsoon: cloud, rain and leeches below 3,000 m.
areas.sleep: Teahouses in Gorak Shep at 5,164 m: very cold, little sleep.

items.name: To Everest Base Camp
items.why: To Gorak Shep, then over the glacier to the base camp at 5,364 m under the Khumbu Icefall, where expeditions camp in April and May.

areas.season: October and November are clear and dry; March to May bring rhododendrons and haze. December to February are cold but clear; June to September is the monsoon: cloud, rain and leeches below 3,000 m.

items.name: Kala Patthar at dawn, then down to Pheriche
items.why: Up by headlamp to 5,644 m for the best view of Everest's summit at sunrise, then down the valley to thicker air.

areas.season: October and November are clear and dry; March to May bring rhododendrons and haze. December to February are cold but clear; June to September is the monsoon: cloud, rain and leeches below 3,000 m.

items.name: Down to Khumjung
items.why: Down the valley to the green Sherpa village above Namche, with the school Edmund Hillary built in 1961 and the monastery that keeps a 'yeti scalp'.

areas.season: October and November are clear and dry; March to May bring rhododendrons and haze. December to February are cold but clear; June to September is the monsoon: cloud, rain and leeches below 3,000 m.

items.name: The last day down to Lukla
items.why: Back over the bridges of the Dudh Kosi to Lukla; flights out leave in the morning and are often delayed by cloud: keep a spare day.

areas.season: Behind the Annapurnas, in their rain shadow: dry even in the monsoon, windy every afternoon. Flights from Pokhara often stop for cloud; the road is the fallback.

items.name: Fly up the Kali Gandaki gorge
items.why: From Pokhara between Dhaulagiri and Annapurna, through one of the deepest gorges on Earth, to the windswept valley of Jomsom.

items.name: Muktinath temple
items.why: At 3,710 m, holy to Hindus and Buddhists: 108 spouts of freezing water and a flame burning out of the rock.

areas.season: Dry and windy, the gate to Upper Mustang.
areas.sleep: Guesthouses in Kagbeni's old mud-brick houses.

items.name: Kagbeni and its red monastery
items.why: A medieval village of tunnels and mud-brick towers where the Kali Gandaki meets the Jhong river, the last stop before the restricted area.

areas.season: At 3,840 m in a desert in the rain shadow: the trekking months are May to October, and it stays dry in the monsoon. The restricted-area permit (US$500 for 10 days) and a licensed guide are required.

items.name: The walled city of Lo
items.why: The capital of the old kingdom of Lo: a mud-walled town with the king's palace and 15th-century monasteries of Jampa and Thubchen, their murals restored.

items.name: Chhoser cave dwellings
items.why: By jeep or horse to cliffs honeycombed with caves cut 2,000 years ago, some five storeys high.

areas.season: Dry and windy in the rain shadow.

items.name: Marpha, the apple village
items.why: Whitewashed Thakali houses on flagstone lanes, a monastery above, and apple brandy from the orchards.
